notes: The options a server owner usually changes, not all of playerbots.conf.dist. default = value in playerbots.conf.dist; default_if_missing = what the code uses when the key is absent; min/max where the code or the meaning bounds the value; coa = option added for Conquest of Azeroth; new_in / changed_in compare with 3.2. Every option needs a world server restart, except those whose description in the .dist says ".reload config". commit = the commit the options were read from; the build itself is identified by its tag.

groups.live: Bots that feel like players (CoA Live)

settings.title: Populate the world automatically
settings.description: Random bots log in when the world server starts. Off: only the bots players add themselves.

settings.title: Minimum online bots
settings.description: Lower bound of the random bot population. 500 is what 16 GB of memory holds comfortably; 5,000 bots use about 9 GB of server memory.

settings.title: Maximum online bots
settings.description: Upper bound of the random bot population; more bots use more CPU and memory. Keep it at or above the minimum.

settings.title: Random bot accounts
settings.description: Accounts that hold the random bots; 0 works out how many are needed.

settings.title: Only while players are online
settings.description: Random bots log out when no real player is online and come back when one logs in.

settings.title: Lowest bot level
settings.description: Lowest level of the random bots.

settings.title: Highest bot level
settings.description: Highest level of the random bots (60 is the Conquest of Azeroth level cap).

settings.title: Conquest of Azeroth classes only
settings.description: Random bots are created only in the 21 Conquest of Azeroth classes, never in the nine WotLK classes.

settings.title: Gather only for skill-ups
settings.description: Gathering bots (herbalism, mining, skinning) skip herbs, veins and corpses that are grey for them and no longer raise their skill. One bot can gather everything again with the chat command "nc +gather all".

settings.title: Races bots never use
settings.description: Comma-separated race ids of the custom races module, added to the always-excluded crashing races below. Only matters when CoACustomRaces.BotsEnable = 1; bots already created keep their race.

settings.title: Custom races that crash the client
settings.description: Always excluded from bots, on top of the list above. Default 32, 72, 77, 97 (Thin Human and Saberon crash a client that sees them, Skyborne has no model), from a race by race client test.

settings.title: Bot surname
settings.description: Random bots carry the surname "Bot" (1), so players tell them from real players at a glance, no surname (0), or a family name of their own (2).

settings.title: Best gear quality
settings.description: Highest item quality random bots get: 2 uncommon, 3 rare, 4 epic.

settings.title: Item level cap
settings.description: Highest item level random bots wear: 78 matches Molten Core, Onyxia and Zul'Gurub gear; 0 = no limit.

settings.title: Level for epic gear
settings.description: With epic quality allowed, the level from which bots may wear epic gear; below it they keep to rare.

settings.title: Chance of lower gear
settings.description: Chance (0 to 1) that an item of a random bot is one quality lower, so not every bot wears the best gear.

settings.title: Your own characters as bots
settings.description: Players may log their own characters in as bots (.playerbots bot add <name>); they keep their own level and gear.

settings.title: Guild members' characters as bots
settings.description: Players may also add the characters of their guild members as bots.

settings.title: Bots per player
settings.description: How many bots one player may control at the same time.

settings.title: Class bots: automatic setup only
settings.description: Players may only use init=auto on their class bots (rebuilt at their level with matching gear); game masters keep every init= command.

settings.title: Recruited bots of the player's faction
settings.description: Bots recruited by a player (lfg bot, .playerbots coa tank|heal|dps, the SquidBots Lite buttons) are of the player's faction.

settings.title: Player-built raids at a time
settings.description: ".playerbots coa raid" fills the raid of whoever types it with bots; players may only build one while the realm has fewer such raids than this. Game masters have no limit.

settings.title: Minutes between two player raids
settings.description: A player may build one raid of bots every so many minutes.

settings.title: Self-found bots roll need on upgrades
settings.description: Self-found bots roll need in dungeons on what is an upgrade for them, greed on the rest; the dungeon simulation gives its loot to the member it upgrades.

settings.title: Log self-found rolls
settings.description: Diagnostic: each roll of a self-found bot in BotLoot.log.

settings.title: Conquest of Azeroth rotations
settings.description: Each Conquest of Azeroth specialization plays its authored rotation and position; off, bots pick spells on their own only.

settings.title: Smart healing
settings.description: Healers heal whoever is under 25% health first and the tank before the others, and pick the heal for how urgent it is.

settings.title: Smart tanking
settings.description: Tanks take first the enemy on the healer, then the one on whoever is lowest, rather than the nearest.

settings.title: Tank bots threat bonus (%)
settings.description: Tank bots cause this much more threat, so that players dealing heavy damage keep under them. 0 = none.

settings.title: Damage dealers keep under the tank (%)
settings.description: Damage dealer bots hold their attacks at this share of the tank threat (20 more at range). 0 = no hold.

settings.title: Coordinated interrupts
settings.description: In a group, one bot kicks each enemy cast and the others keep their interrupt for the next one.

settings.title: Dungeon priorities
settings.description: Bots kick heals and crowd control first; in dungeons they purge boss buffs and enrages, and damage dealers kill healing adds and totems before the boss.

settings.title: Boss mechanics
settings.description: Bots read dungeon and raid casts: they step out of point blank casts, cones and areas while the cast bar runs.

settings.title: Keep passive auras
settings.description: A bot whose level or gear is rebuilt keeps its class passives; without it, it lost them until its next login and did far less damage.

settings.title: Healer mana reserve (%)
settings.description: Share of mana a bot that can heal keeps for healing; under it, it stops spending mana on damage. 0 = no reserve.

settings.title: Reliable attack casting
settings.description: Attacks go through the same cast path as heals: a spell refused for a passing reason is retried soon instead of set aside.

settings.title: Specializations bots never play
settings.description: Conquest of Azeroth specialization ids, comma separated; a bot holding one switches to another of its role.

settings.title: Say which spell is avoided
settings.description: Bots say in chat which enemy spell they step out of ("avoiding Rain of Fire"). Off by default: noisy.

settings.title: Join players' dungeon queues
settings.description: Random bots fill the dungeon finder groups of players.

settings.title: Join players' battleground queues
settings.description: Random bots fill the battleground and arena queues of players.

settings.title: Battlegrounds between bots
settings.description: Random bots also start battlegrounds and arenas by themselves, without players.

settings.title: Duels in front of the capitals
settings.description: Random bots duel outside the main gates of Orgrimmar and Stormwind, in pairs of close levels.

settings.title: Duellists per capital
settings.description: How many bots duel in front of each capital, two per duel (at most 12).

settings.title: Rated 2v2 arenas between bots
settings.description: How many rated 2v2 arenas the bot teams keep going at once. Bot teams also queue when a player joins a rated queue. 0 = none.

settings.title: Rated 3v3 arenas between bots
settings.description: How many rated 3v3 arenas the bot teams keep going at once. Bot teams also queue when a player joins a rated queue. 0 = none.

settings.title: Rated 5v5 arenas between bots
settings.description: How many rated 5v5 arenas the bot teams keep going at once. Bot teams also queue when a player joins a rated queue. 0 = none.

settings.title: Bot arena teams (2v2)
settings.description: Number of 2v2 arena teams of bots, each with a rating from 1000 to 2000 kept between restarts. A bot is in one team at most.

settings.title: Bot arena teams (3v3)
settings.description: Number of 3v3 arena teams of bots, each with a rating from 1000 to 2000 kept between restarts. A bot is in one team at most.

settings.title: Bot arena teams (5v5)
settings.description: Number of 5v5 arena teams of bots, each with a rating from 1000 to 2000 kept between restarts. A bot is in one team at most.

settings.title: High Risk and War Mode bots
settings.description: A share of the random bots plays in High Risk or War Mode (PvP flag on; anyone may attack them, and they attack High Risk and War Mode characters). Off: every bot in PvE.

settings.title: High Risk bots (%)
settings.description: Share of the random bots in High Risk, when the option above is on.

settings.title: War Mode bots (%)
settings.description: Share of the random bots in War Mode, when the option above is on.

settings.title: Gear by activity
settings.description: Random bots wear PvP gear in battlegrounds, arenas and High Risk, PvE gear otherwise, and the item level of the player who groups them.

settings.title: Grouped bots match your item level
settings.description: A bot grouped with a player is geared at the item level of that player. Off: it keeps the gear it has.

settings.title: High Risk bots always in PvP gear
settings.description: High Risk bots wear PvP gear all the time. Off: only in a battleground or an arena, like the other bots.

settings.title: City life
settings.description: Weight of the city visit among the activities of the random bots (10 = about one bot in ten): the bot goes to a capital of its faction, visits the bank, auction house, inn and trainers, then goes back. 0 = never.

settings.title: City visit, shortest (minutes)
settings.description: Shortest stay of a bot visiting a capital.

settings.title: City visit, longest (minutes)
settings.description: Longest stay of a bot visiting a capital.

settings.title: "lfg bot" in chat
settings.description: A player who says "lfg bot heal", "lfg bot tank" or "lfg bot dps" in chat is whispered by free bots of those roles to invite.

settings.title: "lfg bot" level range
settings.description: A bot within this many levels of the player keeps its level and gear; one further away is rebuilt at the player's level.

settings.title: Language of the bots' chat
settings.description: Language of what the bots say in chat (without AI): Auto follows the client language of the players online, or one language for everybody. Nearly all texts exist in French and German; about half in Spanish and Russian.

settings.title: Bots talk
settings.description: Random bots say things in chat now and then.

settings.title: Bot announcements
settings.description: Random bots announce what they do (loot, quests, levels) in the chat channels.

settings.title: "lfg bot" channels
settings.description: Chat channels where bots listen for "lfg bot", comma separated.

settings.title: "lfg bot" reminder (minutes)
settings.description: Every so many minutes, a message to the realm on how to ask the bots. 0 = never.

settings.title: Hide achievements of a bot coming online (minutes)
settings.description: The achievements a random bot earns in its first minutes online stay earned but are not announced (guild, nearby, realm). Never a real player or a player's alts. 0: every achievement announced.

settings.title: One bot achievement announced per (seconds)
settings.description: A random bot announces at most one achievement in this many seconds; the others are earned without a word. Simulated battleground and dungeon credits are never announced. Never a real player or a player's alts. 0: every achievement announced.

settings.title: One bot achievement announced realm-wide per (seconds)
settings.description: On top of the limit per bot: at most one random bot achievement announced in the whole realm in this many seconds (a Server First counts too). Achievements are always earned, only the text is held. Never a real player or a player's alts. 0: no realm limit.

settings.title: Missing dungeon finder role first
settings.description: While a queued party of real players misses a tank or a healer, a free bot of that role queues within seconds instead of at its random roll.

settings.title: Hide level achievements earned again after a restart
settings.description: The server keeps no bot achievement, so after a restart a bot earns them again at its first level-up. A level achievement below the bot's level is then earned without a word. Never a real player or a player's alts.

settings.title: Log bot achievement announces
settings.description: Diagnostic: every hour, the random bot achievements shown and muted and why, in CoaBots.log.

settings.title: Dashboard status file
settings.description: Path of the bot-status.json snapshot the SquidBots dashboard reads (position, health, activity of every bot). Empty = not written.

settings.title: Arena ready pylon
settings.description: A pylon in each arena starting room, as on the original CoA realm: players click it, bots get ready on their own, and the gates open a few seconds after everyone is ready.

settings.title: Arena start once everyone is ready
settings.description: Seconds left before the gates open once every combatant is ready (5-4-3-2-1 shown on screen).

settings.title: Bots prepare before the gates open
settings.description: In the starting room bots buff, call pets and take a spot by role (healers behind, melee in front) facing the gate.

settings.title: Arena kiting
settings.description: Ranged bots and healers step away from melee in arenas instead of standing still, unless they are about to win.

settings.title: Arena focus
settings.description: Damage bots go for the enemy healer, or the lowest enemy in sight, in arenas.

settings.title: Arena pillars
settings.description: Bots under pressure hide behind the arena pillars (Nagrand, Blade’s Edge, Ruins of Lordaeron, Dalaran, Ring of Valor).

settings.title: Duel opening positions
settings.description: During a duel countdown bots take a distance that suits them: close for melee, about 20 yards for ranged.

settings.title: Startup check only
settings.description: The server loads the module and its data, then creates, deletes and logs in no bot. For qualifying a build before opening it; CoA.ValidationMode = 1 does the same.

settings.title: Delete all random bots at the next start
settings.description: Every random bot account and character is deleted at the next start. Set it back to 0 right after that start.

settings.title: Delete random bot guilds at start
settings.description: Random bot guilds are deleted at start, and none is made while it stays on. Back to 0 to resume.

settings.title: Delete random bot arena teams at start
settings.description: Random bot arena teams are deleted at start, and none is made while it stays on. Back to 0 to resume.

settings.title: Dashboard status interval (seconds)
settings.description: Seconds between two snapshots of the dashboard status file.

settings.title: .squidbots why
settings.description: ".squidbots why [name]" on a selected bot tells what it is doing (status, destination, path, last move, how long it has stood still) in the chat and in the why file, to send to the SquidBots team.

settings.title: Why file
settings.description: The file .squidbots why writes to, in the server's logs folder.

settings.title: .squidbots why for game masters only
settings.description: 1: only game master accounts may use .squidbots why; the others are told so.

settings.title: .squidbots why cooldown (seconds)
settings.description: Seconds between two .squidbots why of one player.

settings.title: Bots react like people
settings.description: Random bots greet a player passing by, cheer a level up, bow after a duel and answer, with the lines and emotes of the CoA Live bank (English and French).

settings.title: Bot chat
settings.description: The bots' written chat: zone, world, Trade, LFG, guild, party and say lines, greetings and answers to whispers. Off: they write none of these lines; emotes stay.

settings.title: City life
settings.description: A bot visiting a capital takes a station now and then: it sits at the inn, talks to a banker or an auctioneer, works at an anvil or a forge.

settings.title: Helpful bots
settings.description: A free bot of your faction passing by may raise you when you lie dead, or help in a fight you are losing.

settings.title: Fishing and idle life
settings.description: A bot idling near water now and then goes to the shore and fishes a while.

settings.title: Bots come and go
settings.description: Each bot stays online for a session of a believable length, then logs out while another takes its place.

settings.title: Living bot guilds
settings.description: Bot guilds balanced between the sides, with a message of the day, guild chat and calls for members.

settings.title: Invasions
settings.description: Live invasions announced to the players of their level band, in waves, with a boss and a reward.

settings.title: World PvP of the bots
settings.description: The posts of contested zones send their fighters at each other now and then, and bots defend their capital.

settings.title: Capital raids
settings.description: A faction raid of bots marches on the other side's capital to kill its leader.

settings.title: Bots run dungeons on their own
settings.description: When no real player waits in the Dungeon Finder, five free bots gather and run a classic dungeon of their level.

settings.title: Credible levelling routes
settings.description: A bot sent to a place of its level goes to a zone its side levels in at that level.

settings.title: Bots where the players are
settings.description: For large bot counts with the bot rotation on: the bots online are drawn near the real players.

settings.title: Event log for the dashboard
settings.description: events.jsonl for the SquidBots dashboard: invasions, gold rushes, server firsts, guild news.

settings.title: Auction house bot
settings.description: SquidBots runs the auction house bot (seller and buyer); its settings are the AuctionHouseBot.* keys of mod_ahbot.conf. Set 0 if another auction house bot module is built in. Restart to change it.

settings.title: Bots sell at the auction house
settings.description: Random bots list their loot and crafts at the auction house when they visit it.

settings.title: Bot artisans
settings.description: Bots with a profession craft pieces worth more than their materials and sell them.

settings.title: Craft orders from players
settings.description: A player can ask a bot artisan for a piece by whisper; the bot quotes a price and crafts it.

settings.title: Learned market prices
settings.description: Prices follow the sales seen at the auction house, not only a fixed formula.

settings.title: Bots craft upgrades for themselves
settings.description: A bot with a profession makes for itself the best upgrade among its recipes and wears it. Self-found and classic bots alike.

settings.title: Log crafts for self
settings.description: Diagnostic: each piece a bot makes for itself, in BotLoot.log.

settings.title: Enchanter bots enchant their own gear
settings.description: An enchanter bot puts on a piece it wears the best permanent enchantment it knows, never replacing a better or equal one.

settings.title: Log enchantments for self
settings.description: Diagnostic: each enchantment a bot puts on its own gear, in BotLoot.log.

settings.title: Hourly craft study in a capital
settings.description: Once an hour in a capital, a random bot studies what it could craft or enchant for itself.

settings.title: Minutes between two studies
settings.description: How often a bot studies (at least 5 minutes).

settings.title: Buy missing reagents
settings.description: The study buys the reagents a bot lacks, a vendor's first, the auction house's next. Reagents only, never a finished item. 0: only the reagents it holds.

settings.title: Reagent budget (percent of gold)
settings.description: One study spends at most this share of the bot's gold on reagents.

settings.title: Reagent budget per level (copper)
settings.description: One study spends at most this many copper times the bot's level (2500: 15 gold at level 60).

settings.title: Minimum gain to buy reagents
settings.description: Reagents are bought only when the piece gains at least this percent over what it replaces.

settings.title: Log studies
settings.description: Diagnostic: each study and an hourly count (studies, crafts, enchantments, short of reagents, reagents bought, gold spent) in BotLoot.log.

settings.title: Log auction house buys
settings.description: Diagnostic: each piece or bag a bot buys at the auction house, and an hourly count of self-found and classic bots apart, in BotLoot.log.

settings.title: Bots go to the auction house to buy
settings.description: A bot with nothing to sell still goes to the auction house to buy an upgrade or a bag when it has gold enough, at most once an hour.

settings.title: Shopping budget per level (copper)
settings.description: A bot goes shopping when what it may spend in a visit reaches its level times this many copper (200: 40 silver at level 20, about 2 gold carried).

settings.title: Minutes between two shopping visits
settings.description: Least time between two shopping visits of a bot (at least 5).

settings.title: Bots buy upgrades from afar
settings.description: Random bots buy at their faction's auction house from where they are, once an hour: the best upgrade they can afford, worn at once. Real auctions: the seller is paid.

settings.title: Minutes between two remote buys
settings.description: How often a bot buys from afar (at least 5).

settings.title: Bots list loot from afar
settings.description: Random bots list a few items at their faction's auction house from where they are, every two hours, at the usual price, only when the house pays more than the vendor.

settings.title: Minutes between two remote listings
settings.description: How often a bot lists from afar (at least 5).

settings.title: Items listed from afar
settings.description: Items a bot lists at most from afar each time.

settings.title: Bots per remote trade pass
settings.description: Bots served per pass (one pass every 30 seconds); the others keep their turn for the next pass.

settings.title: Molten Core fixes
settings.description: The CoA Combat fixes to the bots' Molten Core strategy, encounter by encounter.

settings.title: Automatic off-tank
settings.description: In a group with two tanks, the off-tank picks up the loose adds and never taunts what the other tank holds.

settings.title: A player leads the bots
settings.description: The player who opened the Main Tank bar is the bots' main tank in dungeons and raids, without Dungeon Clear.

settings.title: PvP recovery
settings.description: In duels, arenas and battlegrounds a cornered bot can crowd control its attacker, then break away; bandage when safe (CoaPvpBandage).
